edit.description: the chain.ts skeleton, and the written list
the written chain.ts loads as a Chain

summary: Have `flume-harness init` write the chain.ts hop — the factory over the declaration beside it — so an adopted repo can tick.
acceptance: a repo flume-harness init adopted resolves a chain at <configDir>/chain.ts with no hand-written file.
tests: init writes a chain.ts applying the package factory to the declaration beside it
the chain.ts init writes loads through the engine's chain loader as a valid Chain
notes: The engine refuses a load with no `<configDir>/chain.ts`, so init today leaves a repo one file short of a tick. The hop is three lines identical in every consumer — *Verbatim copying is the detector*. The existing skeleton test's tsx-over-shim probe drives the written file through the real loader.

edit.description: the derived set gains the package's own per-run artifacts
the session-capture path stops being module-private
the carve-out goes; both directions close over the whole footprint

summary: Derive the consumer ignore set from the package's own per-run artifacts too, so an adopted repo never hand-adds a line for the package's session captures.
acceptance: an adopted repo carries no untracked state-root path after its first tick, and the ignores test carries no consumer-owned carve-out.
tests: the consumer ignore set names the package's own session capture directory
notes: `consumerIgnores` filters `RUNTIME_IGNORES` by `STATE_ROOT_NAMES`, so a package-owned name is excluded by construction. `SESSIONS_REL` is module-private in `harness/chain.ts` and needs a home `ignores.ts` can import. This repo's `.gitignore` already carries the line — after this the derived set names it, so the test's `CONSUMER_OWNED` carve-out and its stale `.flume/chain.ts` attribution both delete.

edit.description: each phase declares its data keys; the defuse call goes
the shared and build producers name their keys
each slice window names its keys

summary: Declare the package's substituted prompt-arg keys as `promptDataKeys`, derived from the producers that build them, and retire the interim defuse module.
acceptance: no package code neutralizes spans — the engine does it from declared keys — and a key a producer adds without declaring fails the suite.
tests: every prompt-arg key the package's producers return is declared in its phase's promptDataKeys
pins: a substituted value carrying an inline-exec span reaches the agent inert
notes: The engine's list is static and the package's args are computed, so each producer (`sharedPromptArgs`, the three window `args`, `buildPromptArgs`) names its keys beside the map it builds — type the return against them and the sync is structural, not disciplined. A declared key a tick never returns is unused, so over-declaring is safe; an undeclared one loses neutralization silently, which the agreement test catches.

edit.description: what this repo's own chain writes under the state root
the snapshot doc comment names no chain's file

summary: Retire the `.flume/plan/state.md` claim from the code layer: this repo's plan state is the typed artifact, and the engine names no chain's file.
acceptance: nothing under build's fence describes this repo's plan state as `state.md` or as prose scratch.
notes: Two sites, one retired claim. README's *This repo's own chain writes* lists `.flume/plan/state.md` as prose scratch; it is the typed artifact (`spec/harness.md`, *Plan state as declared state*). `src/priorAttempts.ts`'s snapshot doc names it as the loss it prevents — the engine names no chain's file. Out of scope: `docs/CHAIN-AUTHORING.md`, `examples/`, `docs/surveys/`, whose `state.md` is another chain's. No test: prose the package never ships as types.
